parole.testo: From Old High German, compare German Borste, Bavarian burst (“bristle”).

From Old Hungarian, borrowed in the early 11ᵗʰ century from Old High German chafteri (“beehive”) – Middle High German chafter (“beehive; little chamber, closet”), German Käfter (“little chamber, closet”) –, from Medieval Latin capistērium (“beehive”), for scaphistērium, from Ancient Greek σκαφιστήρι

parole.significato: head of cattle, animal of the species Bos taurus
parole.testo: From Old High German marchat (“market”). First attested in 1358.
A wanderword, mainly via German. By metathesis from Old High German biscof, from Latin episcopus.

parole.significato: room (a division of a building enclosed by walls, floor, and ceiling)
parole.testo: From Old High German stuba (“warmed room; oven”).
